text:
I

LOVE


The devilish point descends from heaven

with which you wound and deceive mortal flesh.

It comes smeared with divine tricks,

and heaven and earth join its poison.


The blood of a man that wells in the wound

blossoms into forests: its swelling reeds

of golden shadow split the entrails

of the dark sky, and their ascent asks a question.


In their vain waiting for the answer

the reeds bend their lofty heads.

The sky sets its blue gauzes aflame.


Black winds, behind the glass

of the stars, move great masses

of dead worlds through their outskirts.


II

THE WORK OF LOVE


You see roses and lilies in the thornbush;

you play at being: in one hand you hold,

a little emerald, the ocean;

you speak without a tongue, entangle destiny.


You plant your head in the divine blue

and your feet, antipodes, in the distant

reverse side of the world; and you make yourself sovereign,

and release the sun from its path.


You look at the horizon and your gaze

makes dawn be born in night;

you dream and your fictions create bone.


The hand that raised you in flight falls silent,

and at your feet the sky falls, broken glass,

and dust and shadow lift their heels.


III

LANDSCAPE OF DEAD LOVE


You are sinking now, sun; my waters are colored

with flames about to die; now my unraveled

heart falls, and night brings

edges that weep in the wind.


Already black herds are glimpsed

on opaque shores; already my tongue draws

the pitch of death; and the thorn

no longer turns aside from me; shadows devour me.


Dead hide, the sun lies down at last

like a dog turning upon its tail,

the earth lies down to rest, exhausted.


A bony hand extinguishes the stars:

their stony paths screech

with the black, fleshless pupil.

translation.title: The Devilish Point Descends from Heaven...
translation.editorial_note: The three-part sequence and its typographic labels are preserved; “endiablada punta” is rendered as “devilish point” to retain the poem’s infernal, bodily force.
